title: 1.1 · One object, different readings
bodyHtml:
1.1 · One object, different readings

Materials

Ruler or tape per student or pair; rigid object; removable tape; paper and pencils. No fieldhouse access or caliper required.

55-Minute Sequence

  • 0–5 — Introduce replacement-part problem; students answer first question.
  • 5–10 — Mark endpoints and demonstrate zero/alignment.
  • 10–22 — Every student takes three readings.
  • 22–32 — Compare readings and model the spread calculation.
  • 32–43 — Sketch, hand off, and add missing information.
  • 43–52 — Individual exit ticket in app or on paper.
  • 52–55 — Collect and preview ruler practice.

110-Minute Extension

Use the 55-minute sequence through the sketch. Then 43–55 complete the first explanation; 55–75 repeat with a second tool or observer while holding endpoints constant; 75–90 compare changes in spread; 90–100 revise the drawing; 100–110 write the final exit. Include transitions within these times.

Key

Opening: choice 2. Range check: choice 1. Practice highest 15 11/16, lowest 15 9/16, spread 1/8 in. A fair test changes one factor: for example the observer reads the same tool at the same endpoints directly above and then at an angle. Do not promise a particular result. A systematic offset may remain even with zero spread.

Rating

Rate tr.u1.repeat: 1 = cannot yet identify endpoints/high-low or proposes an unrelated check; 2 = gives a usable spread or plausible cause but needs help with units/control/evidence; 3 = accurate spread with units plus a plausible cause and a controlled check with a predicted discriminating result. Rate sketch separately only from the individual artifact. Use no evidence/not observed rather than inventing a low skill score for absent students.

Fallback

No tool: use the clearly labelled practice readings for reasoning and the drawing task. Do not record instrument-use mastery from supplied data. No internet: paper packet contains the same prompts and scoring criteria.

title: 1.2 · Reading the divisions
bodyHtml:
1.2 · Reading the divisions

Materials

Rulers/tapes, paper, pencils; enlarged reference for 1/32 if tools lack those marks.

55-Minute Sequence

  • 0–8 — Count spaces and identify the smallest division.
  • 8–18 — Model whole inch plus fraction; first checkpoint.
  • 18–35 — Partner reading rounds with role changes.
  • 35–45 — Model nonzero starting point and practice.
  • 45–55 — Individual exit and teacher observation.

Key

Checkpoint 2 5/8 in. Exit start 1 in, end 4 7/16 in, length 3 7/16 in; second reading 2 19/32 in. Prepared calls (whole inch plus tick/denominator): 0+3/16, 1+8/16, 2+12/16, 3+5/16, 0+14/16, 4+1/16, 1+10/16, 2+7/16, 5+15/16, 0+6/16, 1+9/32, 2+16/32, 0+24/32, 3+19/32, 4+31/32. Answers: 3/16, 1 1/2, 2 3/4, 3 5/16, 7/8, 4 1/16, 1 5/8, 2 7/16, 5 15/16, 3/8, 1 9/32, 2 1/2, 3/4, 3 19/32, 4 31/32 inches.

Rating

Observe actual placement and reading. 3 = correct denominator, whole part and unit independently, including a nonzero start; 2 = correct with a cue or an isolated error; 1 = needs modelling to identify divisions. Keep written reasoning and watched skill distinct.

title: 1.3 · The hook and the drawing
bodyHtml:
1.3 · The hook and the drawing

Materials

Sliding-hook tape, ruler or verified rigid reference, paper. Caliper optional. No tool alteration.

55-Minute Sequence

  • 0–10 — Hook diagram and checkpoint.
  • 10–27 — Inspect and compare two setups.
  • 27–35 — Model outside dimensions and inconsistent chain.
  • 35–46 — Sketch and partner reading.
  • 46–55 — Individual exit.

110-Minute Extension

Add 20 minutes of instrument stations, 20 minutes of repeated comparisons and 15 minutes of drawing revision before the exit.

Key

Checkpoint 3. Inconsistent drawing totals 4 1/4 in, exceeding overall by 1/4 in. Exit: reference accuracy, setup, zero/alignment, inside-versus-outside contact or observer reading could explain disagreement. Repeating a result does not establish the cause.

Rating

3 = describes reference and setup checks and distinguishes intended movement from damage; 2 = one usable check with partial explanation; 1 = diagnoses from hook movement alone. Dimensioning target rated separately from drawing.

title: 1.4 · Check it before trusting it
bodyHtml:
1.4 · Check it before trusting it

Materials

At least two instruments and a reference checked by the teacher. If only one tool exists, use supplied Tool A/B/C data for reasoning and observe the one tool in a rotating station.

55-Minute Sequence

  • 0–8 — Three-tool diagnostic and checkpoint.
  • 8–15 — Model the check routine.
  • 15–35 — Inspection/reference stations.
  • 35–45 — Discuss consistent but incorrect readings.
  • 45–55 — Individual exit and feedback.

Key

Checkpoint 1. Tool B offset +1/8 in. Consistency is repeatability, not proof of accuracy. Check zero, alignment, reference validity and another known length. Do not assume subtracting 1/8 fixes every reading without testing.

Rating

3 = records expected/observed values and offset, checks zero/reference, and judges suitability with evidence; 2 = carries out a check with help or incomplete interpretation; 1 = trusts repeated agreement without a reference check.

title: 1.5 · How much can you trust the number?
bodyHtml:
1.5 · How much can you trust the number?

Materials

Tape/rule, object, caliper and feeler gauge if available. Use tool specifications as provided data if an instrument is absent.

55-Minute Sequence

  • 0–10 — Instrument-choice checkpoint and explanation.
  • 10–28 — Five repeat readings.
  • 28–38 — Compare spread and resolution.
  • 38–48 — Individual application to two tasks.
  • 48–55 — Review and self-assess after exit.

110-Minute Extension

Add instrument stations and a revised dimensioned drawing with stated measurement limitations; keep the last 15 minutes for individual exit and self-assessment.

Key

Checkpoint 2. A verified tape/rule may suit the rough layout when its performance supports the tolerance. For the fine gap, a checked suitable feeler gauge or appropriate precision instrument with adequate resolution; do not claim suitability from the instrument name alone. Identical readings show consistency at the observed resolution, not guaranteed accuracy.

Rating

3 = links instrument resolution and verified performance to each task and distinguishes repeatability from accuracy; 2 = suitable choices with incomplete verification/limits; 1 = chooses by familiarity without considering tolerance.

title: 2.1 · The block and its joint
bodyHtml:
2.1 · The block and its joint

Target: tr.u1.nominal; drawing: tr.u1.dimension

Materials

Rule/tape, removable marks, one accessible unit or printed reference.

Fallback

Use the supplied dimensions on paper; assess reasoning, not observed measurement skill.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

B. One block plus the specified joint.

Worked example

Supplied block length 15 5/8 in; joint 3/8 in.
15 5/8 + 3/8 = 16 in. Six modules: 6 x 16 = 96 in.
The nominal module is 16 in. Count joints and define endpoints before predicting a real wall length.

Individual exit key

47 5/8 in; three complete modules would include three joints. The missing joint accounts for 3/8 in.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. Record physical skill only from observed performance; absence or no evidence is not a fabricated low skill score.

title: 2.2 · Identify the material before the size
bodyHtml:
2.2 · Identify the material before the size

Target: tr.u1.nominal; drawing: tr.u1.dimension

Materials

Detached labelled copper and EMT samples; caliper or reference cards.

Fallback

Compare supplied dimensions and a drawn section; keep caliper skill unobserved.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

B. No; identify the material and consult its dimensions.

Worked example

Supplied Type L copper: OD 0.625 in, wall 0.040 in.
ID = 0.625 - 2(0.040) = 0.545 in.
The inside diameter is 0.545 in in this reference; it is not the nominal label.

Individual exit key

0.706 - 0.625 = 0.081 in. Both ODs exceed 0.500 in; fittings and required clearance also matter.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. Record physical skill only from observed performance; absence or no evidence is not a fabricated low skill score.

title: 2.3 · Gauge, diameter and area
bodyHtml:
2.3 · Gauge, diameter and area

Target: tr.u1.gauge; drawing: tr.u1.sketch

Materials

Bare disconnected labelled wire; caliper; calculator.

Fallback

Use reference areas and supplied diameters; do not claim actual caliper performance.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

C. Four, so area is about 2.53 times as large.

Worked example

Provided conductor diameter d = 2.00 mm.
A = pi x d² / 4 = pi x 4 / 4.
A is about 3.14 mm²; diameter and area have different units.

Individual exit key

3.31/2.08 is about 1.59, a two-step ratio. Three decreasing AWG steps approximately double area. Check bare diameter, caliper zero, contact pressure and sample identity.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. Record physical skill only from observed performance; absence or no evidence is not a fabricated low skill score.

title: 2.4 · Four names, four conventions
bodyHtml:
2.4 · Four names, four conventions

Target: tr.u1.vocab; drawing: tr.u1.dimension

Materials

Four labelled sample cards; ruler if samples available.

Fallback

All four may be paper cards with supplied values.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

B. Compare it with the applicable actual-size specification, not the nominal name.

Worked example

Specified width 3.500 in, allowed +/-0.125 in; measured 3.5625 in.
Deviation = 3.5625 - 3.500 = +0.0625 in. Allowed interval = 3.375 to 3.625 in.
The reading is inside this supplied interval.

Individual exit key

Nominal 2x4; actual measured 1.5 x 3.5 in. Need applicable size specification/tolerance and measurement confidence; nominal name alone is insufficient.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. title: 2.5 · Does it fit at the stated scale?
bodyHtml:
2.5 · Does it fit at the stated scale?

Target: tr.u1.fits; drawing: tr.u1.scale

Materials

Cardboard channel or paper; ruler; circle template.

Fallback

Use the supplied dimensions and draw on paper; no fieldhouse visit required.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

B. Outside envelope including the supplied sleeve.

Worked example

Dry mockup depth 3.500 in; sleeve envelope 2.750 in; pipe OD 2.375 in.
Remaining space = 3.500 - 2.750 = 0.750 in. Centered side gaps = 0.375 in each.
The sleeve fits this empty mockup geometrically. A real wall requires its approved structural/service detail.

Individual exit key

No. Required depth = 2.750 + 1.000 = 3.750 in, a 0.250-inch shortfall. Drawing at 1:2 needs 1.875 inches for that depth.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. Record physical skill only from observed performance; absence or no evidence is not a fabricated low skill score.

title: 3.1 · Chain and datum layout
bodyHtml:
3.1 · Chain and datum layout

Target: tr.u1.cumul; drawing: tr.u1.datum

Materials

Tape, removable marks, 12-foot accessible run.

Fallback

Use a 36-inch model with nine 4-inch intervals; compare methods without requiring a detectable error.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

A. 144 in.

Worked example

Nine 16-inch intervals; each interval has a supplied +1/16-inch systematic offset.
9 x 16 = 144 in; 9 x 1/16 = 9/16 in.
Under this stated model, the final chain mark is 144 9/16 in.

Individual exit key

1/4 divided by nine is 1/36 inch average signed interval deviation if endpoints and interval count are correct. It does not prove equal individual errors. Check each interval and reference measurement.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. Record physical skill only from observed performance; absence or no evidence is not a fabricated low skill score.

title: 3.2 · Why the centerline matters
bodyHtml:
3.2 · Why the centerline matters

Target: tr.u1.sixteen; drawing: tr.u1.dimension

Materials

Paper/cardboard strips, ruler, pencil.

Fallback

Use scaled paper strips and label real dimensions.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

A. Stud width and the chosen edge affect the position.

Worked example

Sheet width 48 in; support centers 16 in apart.
48/16 = 3 intervals; centers at 0, 16, 32 and 48 in.
Four center positions bound three intervals.

Individual exit key

14.5 in clear gap, assuming parallel equal-width supports. Center spacing includes one full support width; do not use 16 in as the clear opening.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. title: 3.3 · Estimate it, then align the views
bodyHtml:
3.3 · Estimate it, then align the views

Target: tr.u1.views; drawing: tr.u1.views

Materials

Box or block, ruler, squared paper.

Fallback

Use the supplied box dimensions; assess drawing interpretation, not inaccessible-site measurement.

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.

Opening key

A. Their corresponding width.

Worked example

Six complete modules at a supplied 16 in each.
Estimated span = 6 x 16 = 96 in.
96 in is a model estimate until checked; partial modules or extra joints change it.

Individual exit key

The right view should be 3 deep x 4 high. It repeats the front width instead of the depth. Direction labels resolve the ambiguity.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. title: 3.4 · Make a defensible tolerance call
bodyHtml:
3.4 · Make a defensible tolerance call

Target: tr.u1.tolerance; drawing: tr.u1.dimension

Materials

Paper number lines, ruler, cardboard strips; no cutting precision metal gauges.

Fallback

Use supplied readings as exact for arithmetic and state their real-measurement limits.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.
7-17 Teach the model and work the numerical example.
17-35 Investigation and individual record.
35-45 Draw, exchange and clarify the handoff.
45-55 Individual exit; identify one next step.

110-minute extension

Extend the investigation by 25 minutes for repeated trials or a second method, add 20 minutes for comparison and drawing revision, and reserve an extra 10 minutes for individual feedback. Do not invent additional results to fill time.

Opening key

A. 15 15/16 to 16 1/16 in.

Worked example

Target 16 in +/-1/16 in; reading 16 1/8 in.
Upper limit = 16 1/16. Reading - upper = 1/16 in.
The supplied exact reading is out by 1/16 in; its deviation from target is +1/8 in.

Individual exit key

47 7/8 to 48 1/8 in. Deviation -3/16 in; out below by 1/16 in. Check zero/reference, resolution, endpoints or repeatability appropriate to the task.

Evidence rating

3: an accurate, evidence-linked response matching the key, with quantities/units and an appropriate check. 2: a usable approach with one material omission or teacher cue. 1: an unsupported or incorrect approach needing instruction. title: 3.5 · Mastery: inspect and revise the bay
bodyHtml:
3.5 · Mastery: inspect and revise the bay

Target: tr.u1.asbuilt; drawing: tr.u1.asbuilt

Materials

Case A pages, rule, graph paper; optional pre-surveyed classroom mockup.

Fallback

Use provided survey; score interpretation and drawings, with physical measurement marked not observed.

55-minute sequence

0-7 Individual diagnostic choice; discuss the evidence needed.

Opening key

B. The supported observed number with source and revision note.

Worked example

Example target 48 +/-1/8 in; supplied reading 48 1/16 in.
Allowed interval 47 7/8 to 48 1/8; deviation +1/16.
Inside the supplied interval. This arithmetic alone does not demonstrate instrument skill.

Individual exit key

Use Case A key. Opening width and left offset fail the supplied interval; service OD note is incorrect. Accept a different priority if tied to a supported consequence. Require evidence source and limits.

Evidence rating
